judgments.reasoning_cat1: The note states that if the Owner predeceases the Insured ownership passes to the deceased Owner's estate unless a Contingent Owner is named, but it is cast as a 'NOTE' rather than an operative term, leaving unclear whether it is a binding default rule or mere instruction. 'Such result is not desired' is an odd, subjective trigger for a property-succession default.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against the Contingent Owner designation line (item b) and the beneficiary designation provisions; here the Insured and Owner appear to be the same person, so the default never bites and nothing else in the instrument contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It is a filling-in instruction ('list name and reason in Special Requests') rather than a promissory term, and the exclusion mechanism for an excluded spouse is never spelled out. The vagueness of what an entry in 'Special Requests' legally accomplishes is a latent but unexercised defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against the Plan of Insurance riders block (Family Plan — Spouse & Children's Rider) and the Special Requests box; no family term coverage was elected on this application, so the instruction is inert.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: This is the core representation clause and it reads that 'only false statement or material misrepresentation therein MAY result in loss of coverage' — 'may' is permissive rather than mandatory, 'material' is undefined, and the 'only/any' word is exactly the kind of one-word slip that changes meaning. A coverage-rescission fight would turn on precisely these words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against c004 ('true and complete to the best of my knowledge and belief'), c008 (statements must 'remain true ... without material change') and c012 (agent certifies he accurately recorded the answers); the knowledge-qualified standard in c004 and the agent's recording certification pull against a flat forfeiture for any false statement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To the best of my knowledge and belief' qualifies the truthfulness warranty in a way that is classically construed against strict warranty, and 'will be the basis of any policy issued' is not the same as being incorporated into or made part of the policy. Both phrases are standard battlegrounds in rescission litigation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against c003 (which speaks of 'false statement or material misrepresentation' without the knowledge qualifier), c008 (condition that answers remain true) and c020 ('A copy of this application will ...'); the knowledge-and-belief limit and the absolute conditions in c008 do not sit comfortably together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It acknowledges receipt of, and accepts the terms of, a separate Limited Temporary Insurance Agreement whose terms are nowhere set out, so the obligations assumed are indeterminate on the face of the clause. The conditional link to 'payment shown in Question 5' adds a further contingency.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against c006, which carves out 'except as provided in my Temporary Insurance Agreement' from the no-coverage-until-delivery rule; the incorporated document is not part of this instrument, which leaves the interaction of the two clauses unresolvable from the contract alone.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause states that except as provided in the Temporary Insurance Agreement no policy shall be in force 'unless and until' enumerated conditions are met, and the enumeration is a conjunctive list whose reach and the delivery condition are the usual point of dispute. The exception itself is defined by reference to an absent document.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against c005 (acceptance of the Limited Temporary Insurance Agreement) and c008 (the continuation of the conditions); the exception for temporary insurance and the absolute 'no policy in force' rule can be read to conflict about when risk attaches.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: This is a statutorily prescribed fraud warning rather than a bargained term, and its operative content is a criminal-law statement, not a coverage rule. There is little for a court to construe in it as a contract term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against c011 and c019, the other fraud warnings in the same instrument; they are duplicative and consistent, and none of them purports to alter the coverage conditions in c003–c008.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Condition (3) — that the statements and answers 'remain true and complete, without material change, as of the date of' delivery — imports an undefined materiality standard and a continuing-truth obligation running to an unspecified date. Condition (2), full first premium paid 'during the lifetime of all persons to be insured', is another commonly litigated trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against c004, which limits the applicant's representation to the best of his knowledge and belief, and against c003; a continuing warranty of no material change is hard to reconcile with a knowledge-qualified representation made at signing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Acceptance of a policy is deemed agreement to 'any corrections, additions or changes' made by the insurer and noted in the Home Office Endorsements — a broad, insurer-drafted catch-all whose outer limit ('any changes') is undefined. The concluding words about agreeing 'to be in writing' are garbled enough to obscure what is required.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against c010 (no agent may make or change a contract of insurance) and the 'For Home Office Use Only — Home Office Endorsements' box, which is blank on this application; nothing else contradicts the clause but it depends on a section never filled in.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause lists specific agent disabilities (make or change a contract, extend a premium due date, waive rights) and trails off, leaving a general-vs-specific question about what else the agent cannot do. It is also drafted wholly in the insurer's favour, the classic setting for contra proferentem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against c012, in which the agent certifies he 'truly and accurately recorded' the applicant's answers, and against c036 (no one authorized to change risk class); if the agent misrecorded answers, this no-authority clause and the agent's certification point in opposite directions on imputed knowledge.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A prescribed statutory fraud-penalty notice; it creates no contractual right or duty and its terms track the statute. Nothing in it invites competing readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against c007 and c019, the parallel fraud warnings; all three are cumulative and none conflicts with the representation and condition clauses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The agent certifies he 'truly and accurately recorded' the information 'supplied by the Applicant and/or Proposed Insured', which raises the standard question of whose statement an answer on the form is. 'Truly and accurately recorded' is not the same as 'the answers are true'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against c003 (the joint representation of Insured and Agent) and c010 (agent has no authority to bind or waive); the certification arguably attributes recording errors to the insurer's agent while c010 disclaims the agent's authority, a real tension in a rescission dispute.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The authorization runs to a long enumerated list of recipients closing with 'and/or employer', then authorizes release of 'any and all information, records or knowledge which you have' — an unbounded catch-all against enumerated specifics. The breadth of 'any and all ... knowledge' has no discernible limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against c017 (which extends the same authorization to financial, employment and personal information) and c025 (the medical-exam form version, which omits the financial extension); the two versions do not describe identical scopes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Good, as needed, for 24 months from the date signed or while I have a claim, if longer' contains two vague operators — 'as needed' and an open-ended extension for so long as a claim exists. When the authorization expires is therefore not fixed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against c023, the identically worded duration clause on the medical examiner's form; the two are consistent, so no internal conflict emerges.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line administrative statement that a photocopy may be used as the original; it has no operative content beyond evidentiary convenience. Nothing in the phrasing is capable of two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against c024, the same statement on the medical-exam form; they match and neither is contradicted elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare acknowledgment of receipt of the Notice of Information Practices, with no promissory content. There is nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against c013 and c018 (the authorization and release provisions); the acknowledgment is consistent with them and the Notice itself is not part of this instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: After enumerating medical categories the clause adds that the recipient 'may also give ... financial, employment or personal information' — 'personal information' is an open-ended residual sitting against a detailed medical list. The reach of that residual category is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against c025, the medical-exam-form authorization, which covers only physical or mental condition and omits financial and employment information; the two authorizations executed in the same transaction describe different scopes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The permitted recipients include 'others who perform business or legal services related to my application or the policy', a catch-all beyond the named reinsurers and MIB, and non-release is subject to 'required or permitted by law'. 'Permitted by law' swallows much of the promised confidentiality.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against c022, the identical release clause on the medical-exam form, and c013; they are consistent with each other, so no internal contradiction appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Another prescribed fraud warning on the Part 2 application, purely declaratory of criminal exposure. It imposes no contractual obligation capable of competing constructions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against c007 and c011; the warnings repeat rather than conflict, and none modifies the Part 1 representation clauses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is truncated at 'A copy of this application will' so its operative promise — attachment to, or incorporation in, the policy — is missing from the face of the provision. An incomplete operative sentence is precisely the sort of mechanical defect that changes meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against c004, which says a copy of the application 'will be the basis of any policy issued'; whether the Part 2 medical application is likewise made part of the policy matters directly to any misrepresentation defence and is not resolved elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The addressee list ends with a bare 'or employer' after a string of medical and insurance entities, leaving the general category's reach uncertain, and the text as printed interleaves two different paragraphs. The result is a provision whose sentence boundaries are not determinable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against c013, the Part 1 authorization addressee list; the two lists are broadly parallel, and the differences are minor rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It permits release to 'others who perform business or legal services related to my application or the policy' — an undefined residual class — and conditions confidentiality on what is 'required or permitted by law'. Those two open terms are the only construable content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against c018, the identically worded release clause in the Part 1 authorization; they agree, so the duplication creates no incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Good, as needed, for 24 months ... or while I have a claim, if longer' leaves both the trigger ('as needed') and the end date indeterminate. The extension for the life of a claim has no outer bound.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against c014, the Part 1 duration clause, which is worded identically; no conflict arises between them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A boilerplate statement that a photocopy may serve as the original; no term in it bears two meanings. The garbling is a scanning artefact rather than a drafting one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against c015, its Part 1 counterpart; the two are the same and consistent with the rest of the authorization.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grant covers 'any and all information, records or knowledge ... about my physical or mental condition', an unbounded formula followed by an illustrative list of medical categories. The relationship between the general grant and the enumerated illustrations is the only construable feature.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against c013 and c017, the Part 1 authorization, which additionally reaches financial, employment and personal information; the medical-exam version is narrower, so the applicant signed two authorizations of different scope in one transaction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It says the rider allows payment of a portion of the death proceeds before death and that accepting a payment 'reduces the death benefit the beneficiary will receive', but the size, method and qualifying conditions of the reduction are stated only by cross-reference. 'A portion' is left undefined in the provision itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against c027 (Limitations) and the hypothetical example showing $150,000 reduced to $95,884, and against the Statement of Policy Cost showing a $100,000 benefit amount with an Accelerated Benefit Rider at 'No Charge'; the illustration's face amount does not match the policy's, which is an inconsistency across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: This is a mandated consumer disclosure in plain terms — not long-term care insurance, may be insufficient, usable for any purpose — with no operative promise to construe. 'May not be enough' is hedged but is a warning, not an obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against c026 (description of the rider) and c029 (Medicaid/SSI); the disclosures are mutually consistent and none creates a benefit that this clause takes away.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure recommendation to consult a tax advisor, imposing no duty on either party. There is nothing capable of two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against c035 ('Ohio National Life does not give legal or tax advice'); the two reinforce rather than contradict each other.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The statement that mere ownership 'will not in and of itself' affect eligibility is carefully hedged, and the accompanying advice to consult the Medicaid Unit is directory. The hedge makes it hard to read as a promise at all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against c027 and c026; the accelerated-benefit disclosures are consistent, and nothing elsewhere promises anything about government benefit eligibility.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A request that the policyholder review the policy and the attached copy of the application; it is hortatory and creates no obligation. Nothing in it is ambiguous in a way that matters.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against c004 ('a copy of this application will be the basis of any policy issued') and c020; the reference to a copy of the application at the back of the policy is consistent with those clauses and in fact corroborates attachment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The free-look right is described only as 'a limited number' of days, with the actual period relegated to the policy's cover page, so the provision as written fixes no ascertainable deadline. A right whose duration is stated as 'limited' is vague on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against the policy cover pages and the Statement of Policy Cost and Benefit Information in this instrument; the referenced cover-page detail on the return period does not appear anywhere in the documents produced, leaving the cross-reference dangling.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Dividends, when applicable' and dependence on Ohio National's investments and the 'current scale', coupled with 'they are not guaranteed', leaves the entitlement discretionary and its measure undefined. The 'when applicable' qualifier is doing a great deal of unstated work.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against the policy cover page describing this as a 'Renewable Term Life Insurance Policy — Nonparticipating' and against c033; a nonparticipating policy pays no dividends at all, so a dividend provision in the same instrument is genuinely hard to reconcile.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause describes dividend options ('as much term insurance as the dividend will buy') and says the cost of the additional benefits is shown 'at current rates. Such rates are not guaranteed', so the actual benefit is indeterminate. The conditional 'if [this] option is shown' further defers content to a document elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against the 'Nonparticipating' designation on the policy cover page and against c032 and the Plan of Insurance dividend-option boxes on the application; a dividend-option provision cannot easily coexist with a nonparticipating term policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is a fragment ('Insurance issued by Ohio National Life Assurance ... payable') and does not state a complete proposition, so what it asserts about the issuing company cannot be read off the text. That incompleteness is itself a mechanical defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against the application header, which offers a choice between The Ohio National Life Insurance Company and Ohio National Life Assurance Corporation, and against the Statement of Policy Cost, which names Ohio National Life Assurance Corporation; the identity of the contracting insurer is stated inconsistently across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A disclaimer that the insurer gives no legal or tax advice and a direction to consult a professional; it is standard and single-meaning. Nothing turns on any particular word.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against c028 (the tax-advisor recommendation on the accelerated benefits form); the two disclaimers agree, and nothing else in the instrument purports to give tax advice.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'No one is authorized to make any change to your policy's risk class or rating' is an absolute prohibition that, read literally, would bind the insurer itself as well as its agents. 'No one' is unqualified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against c010 (no agent may change a contract of insurance or waive Ohio National's rights) and c009 (the insured agrees to any corrections or changes made by Ohio National and noted in Home Office Endorsements); c009 expressly contemplates insurer changes, which sits awkwardly with an absolute 'no one'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pointer to the Life Insurance Buyers Guide for an explanation of the cost indices; it is informational and creates no right. Its only flaw is that the sentence is incomplete as printed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against the Surrender Cost Index and Net Payment Index figures in the Statement of Policy Cost; the pointer is consistent with them and the Buyers Guide is not part of this instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision is fragmentary — values 'are affected by the risk class and rating, if any' followed by a broken reference to representations concerning 'any possible future' rating — so its subject and its prohibition are both incomplete. What is forbidden and to whom cannot be determined from the words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against c036 (no one authorized to change risk class or rating) and the 'Risk Class*: Preferred Nonsmoker' entry; the two clauses cover overlapping ground consistently, so the difficulty is intrinsic rather than relational.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Premiums may change annually thereafter' uses a permissive 'may' about an insurer's right to raise the price, with the baseline year and the limit on any change left to a truncated cross-reference. Whether 'may change' means may increase without limit is exactly the sort of question a court would have to resolve.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against the policy cover pages stating 'Premiums Subject to Change' and 'Premiums Subject to Guaranteed Maximum Premiums', and against the stated Annual Premium of $132.00; a guaranteed-maximum representation and an open right to change annually are in tension.
